newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds hold the spread to U.S..
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds hold the spread to U.S..

text.p: The Australian bond market lost some ground against Canadian and New Zealand debt, but yield spreads held steady against the U.S. after Monday's narrowing.

Traders said the local market is likely to be steered by the moods of the U.S. Treasuries until Thursday's Australian labour force report, where a weak number could see the market building up a case for a further easing in monetary policy.

"The labour market will be the key to the next move in official interest rates. Forward indicators for labour demand suggest employment growth is running well below official expectations and we believe that this will lead to a rate cut in October/November," said Nigel Stapledon, chief economist at Westpac.

The Canadian market played catch up to the global debt rally that followed Friday's U.S. payrolls data, which while strong, suggested that the Fed might not tighten policy too aggressively when the FOMC meets on September 24.
New Zealand bonds were supported by a successful T-bill tender and there was some bullishness ahead of this Friday's RBNZ report of economic projections.
